topics.content:
GOD GIVES HIS LAW TO US: REASONS GOD GIVES HIS LAW TO US, PURPOSE OF LAW AND THE TEN COMMANDMENTS
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 9
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Is the Giver of Law: Meaning of Law, Differences Between Laws and Rules, and Reasons Why Laws Were Given | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 8 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD GIVES HIS LAW TO US
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. God Gives His Law to Us and Reasons God Gives His Law to Us
3. Purpose of God’s Law
4. The Ten Commandments and Meaning of Some of the Commandments
5. Importance of Obeying God’s Law
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain why God gives His laws to us.
2. State the purposes of God’s laws.
3. Explain the meaning of the Ten Commandments.
4. Mention the Ten Commandments.
5. State the importance of obeying God’s laws.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God is the giver of law and that laws and rules guide people’s behaviour and promote peace and order.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils why God gives His laws and the Ten Commandments.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2.Chart showing the Ten Commandments
3. Pictures of Moses receiving the commandments
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God gives His laws to guide His people and teach them how to live according to His will. His laws help us know what is right and wrong and show us how to love God and other people.
God’s laws also help people to live peacefully, avoid wrongdoing and develop good character. One important set of laws given by God is the Ten Commandments.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the reasons God gives His laws to us, the purpose of the law, and the Ten Commandments.
GOD GIVES HIS LAW TO US
God gives His laws to guide His people and teach them how to live according to His will. His laws help us know what is right and wrong and show us how to love God and other people.
REASONS GOD GIVES HIS LAW TO US
God gives His laws to guide us and help us live according to His will. He gives His laws to:
1. Guide us to do what is right.
2. Teach us the difference between right and wrong.
3. Help us obey God and follow His instructions.
4. Promote love and respect among people.
5. Protect us from wrongdoing and harmful behaviour.
6. Promote peace and good behaviour in society.
PURPOSE OF GOD’S LAW
The purpose of God’s law is to:
1. Help us live according to God’s will.
2. Teach us to love God and other people.
3. Guide our behaviour.
4. Help us develop good character.
5. Promote justice, peace and fairness.
6. Help us live well with one another.
THE TEN COMMANDMENTS
The Ten Commandments are ten important laws that God gave the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
They are:
1. You shall have no other gods before Me.
2. You shall not make idols.
3. You shall not misuse the name of the Lord your God.
4. Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
5. Honour your father and your mother.
6. You shall not kill.
7. You shall not commit adultery.
8. You shall not steal.
9. You shall not give false testimony against your neighbour.
10. You shall not covet.
Bible Reference: Exodus 20:1-17.
Lesson - God’s laws guide us to love God, obey Him, do what is right, respect others and live peacefully. We should therefore make every effort to obey God’s laws.
MEANING OF THE COMMANDMENT
1. Have no other gods: Worship God alone.
2. Do not make idols: Do not worship images or other gods.
3. Do not misuse God’s name: Use God’s name with respect.
4. Keep the Sabbath holy: Set aside the Sabbath for God.
5. Honour your parents: Respect and obey your parents.
6. Do not kill: Do not deliberately take another person’s life.
7. Do not commit adultery: Do not have sexual relations with another person’s spouse.
8. Do not steal: Do not take what belongs to another person.
9. Do not give false testimony: Always tell the truth.
10. Do not covet: Do not wrongly desire what belongs to another person.
IMPORTANCE OF OBEYING GOD’S LAW
Obeying God’s laws:
1. Pleases God.
2. Helps us live rightly.
3. Promotes peace.
4. Builds good character.
5. Helps us respect others.
6. Prevents wrongdoing.
7. Strengthens our relationship with God.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Why does God give His laws to us?
A. To make us unhappy
B. To guide us to do what is right
C. To make us afraid
D. To stop us from learning
2. God’s law teaches us the difference between ______.
A. right and wrong
B. young and old
C. rich and poor
D. big and small
3. What does God’s law help us to do?
A. Disobey God
B. Ignore others
C. Fight with others
D. Obey God
4. Who received the Ten Commandments from God?
A. Abraham
B. David
C. Moses
D. Jacob
5. Where did God give the Ten Commandments to Moses?
A. Mount Bethlehem
B. Mount Carmel
C. Mount Jordan
D. Mount Sinai
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God gives His laws to guide us to do what is ______.
7. God’s law teaches us the difference between right and ______.
8. The Ten Commandments were given to the Israelites through ______.
9. God gave the Ten Commandments on Mount ______.
10. We should ______ God’s laws.
C. True or False
11. God gives His laws to guide His people.
12. God’s laws encourage people to do wrong.
13. The Ten Commandments were given through Moses.
14. God’s laws promote peace and good behaviour.
15. We should disobey God’s laws.
D. Matching
16. God’s Law - A. A day kept holy
17. Moses - B. Doing what God instructs
18. Ten Commandments - C. God’s instructions for His people
19. Obedience - D. Laws given by God to the Israelites
20. Sabbath - E. Received the Ten Commandments
ANSWER KEY
1. B 2. A 3. D 4. C 5. C
6. right
7. wrong
8. Moses
9. Sinai
10. obey
11. True
12. False
13. True
14. True
15. False
16. God’s Law - C. God’s instructions for His people
17. Moses - E. Received the Ten Commandments
18. Ten Commandments - D. Laws given by God to the Israelites
19. Obedience - B. Doing what God instructs
20. Sabbath - A. A day kept holy
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that God gives His laws to guide His people, teach them right from wrong, promote love and respect, protect them from wrongdoing and help them live peacefully with others.
Pupils also learned that the Ten Commandments are important laws given by God to the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai. Obeying God’s laws pleases God, builds good character and helps us live rightly.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- Why do we need laws?
- Who gives laws to His people?
- What do you know about the Ten Commandments?
The teacher explains that God gives His laws to guide His people and help them live according to His will.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention what they know about God’s laws.
Step 2: Reasons God Gives His Law to Us
The teacher explains that God gives His laws to:
- Guide us to do what is right.
- Teach us the difference between right and wrong.
- Help us obey Him.
- Promote love and respect.
- Protect us from wrongdoing.
- Promote peace and good behaviour.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention reasons why God gives His laws.
Step 3: Purpose of God’s Law
The teacher explains that the purpose of God’s law is to:
- Help us live according to God’s will.
- Teach us to love God and others.
- Guide our behaviour.
- Help us develop good character.
- Promote justice, peace and fairness.
- Help us live well with one another.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention and explain some purposes of God’s law.
Step 4: The Ten Commandments
The teacher explains that the Ten Commandments are ten important laws given by God to the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
The teacher introduces the Ten Commandments:
- You shall have no other gods before Me.
- You shall not make idols.
- You shall not misuse the name of the Lord your God.
- Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
- Honour your father and your mother.
- You shall not kill.
- You shall not commit adultery.
- You shall not steal.
- You shall not give false testimony against your neighbour.
- You shall not covet.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen, read and repeat the Ten Commandments after the teacher.
Step 5: Meaning of the Ten Commandments
The teacher explains the commandments in simple terms:
- Have no other gods: Worship God alone.
- Do not make idols: Do not worship images or other gods.
- Do not misuse God’s name: Use God’s name with respect.
- Keep the Sabbath holy: Set aside the Sabbath for God.
- Honour your parents: Respect and obey your parents.
- Do not kill: Do not deliberately take another person’s life.
- Do not steal: Do not take what belongs to another person.
- Do not give false testimony: Always tell the truth.
- Do not covet: Do not desire what belongs to another person wrongly.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the commandments in their own words.
Step 6: Importance of Obeying God’s Law
The teacher explains that obeying God’s laws:
- Pleases God.
- Helps us do what is right.
- Promotes peace.
- Builds good character.
- Helps us respect others.
- Prevents wrongdoing.
- Strengthens our relationship with God.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the importance of obeying God’s laws.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Mention five reasons God gives His laws.
- Group 2: Mention five purposes of God’s law.
- Group 3: Mention the Ten Commandments.
- Group 4: Mention five benefits of obeying God’s laws.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the reasons God gives His laws, the purpose of the law and the Ten Commandments. The teacher gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
God Reveals Himself to Us: Purpose of God’s Revelation, the Call of Samuel, and Ways God Reveals Himself to His People | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 10 Christian Religious Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Why does God give His laws to us?
2. Mention five purposes of God’s law.
3. What are the Ten Commandments?
4. Who received the Ten Commandments from God?
5. Mention five benefits of obeying God’s laws.

topics.title: God Is the Giver of Law: Meaning of Law, Differences Between Laws and Rules, and Reasons Why Laws Were Given | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 8 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD IS THE GIVER OF LAW: MEANING OF LAW, DIFFERENCE BETWEEN LAWS AND RULES, AND REASONS WHY LAWS WERE GIVEN
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 8
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Calls for a Purpose: Purpose of God’s Call, Response to God’s Call, and Benefits of God’s Call | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 6 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD IS THE GIVER OF LAW
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Law
3. Examples of God’s Laws
4. Difference between Law and Rule
5. Why God Gave Laws
6. Importance of Obeying God’s Laws
7. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
8. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of law.
2. Explain the meaning of rules.
3. State differences between laws and rules.
4. Mention reasons why laws were given.
5. Explain why people should obey laws.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God calls His people for a purpose and that people should respond to God’s call with faith and obedience.
This lesson teaches pupils that God also gives laws and instructions to guide His people to live rightly.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Charts showing laws and rules
3. Flashcards
4. Pictures of people obeying laws
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God gives laws to guide His people and teach them how to live good and responsible lives. Laws help people know what is right and wrong and guide them in their relationship with God and with one another.
Laws and rules are important in our homes, schools, communities and countries. Although they are related, laws and rules are not exactly the same. People are expected to obey laws and rules in order to promote peace and order.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the meaning of law, the differences between laws and rules, and the reasons why laws were given.
MEANING OF LAW
A law is an official instruction or set of instructions made by an authority to guide people’s behaviour and maintain peace and order.
God is the giver of laws to His people. God’s laws teach us how to live rightly, obey Him and treat other people well.
EXAMPLES OF GOD’S LAWS
Some of God’s laws include:
1. You shall have no other gods before Me.
2. You shall not make idols.
3. You shall not misuse the name of God.
4. Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
5. Honour your father and your mother.
6. You shall not kill.
7. You shall not commit adultery.
8. You shall not steal.
9. You shall not give false testimony against others.
10. You shall not covet what belongs to others.
These laws are known as the Ten Commandments, which God gave to the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
Bible Reference: Exodus 20:1-17.
MEANING OF RULES
A rule is an instruction that tells people what they should or should not do in a particular place, group, or situation.
Rules help to maintain order, discipline, safety, and good behaviour.
Examples of rules:
- Pupils should come to school on time.
- Pupils should keep the classroom clean.
- Pupils should listen when the teacher is teaching.
- Pupils should not fight in school.
DIFFERENCES BETWEEN LAWS and RULES
1. Laws are official instructions made by the government, while rules are instructions made by a school, family, organisation or group.
2. Laws usually apply to people in a country, state or community, while rules usually apply to members of a particular group or people in a particular place.
3. Breaking a law can lead to legal punishment, while breaking a rule usually leads to consequences set by the group or organisation.
4. Laws help maintain peace, order and justice in society, while rules help maintain discipline and order in a particular place or group.
5. Laws are enforced by government authorities, while rules are enforced by the people or authorities responsible for the group or place.
Simple Example
- Law: People must obey traffic laws when using the road.
- Rule: Pupils must not make noise during a lesson.
In simple terms: A law is an official requirement that applies to society, while a rule is an instruction that guides behaviour in a particular group or place.
WHY GOD GAVE LAWS
God gave laws to:
1. Guide His people.
2. Teach them what is right and wrong.
3. Help them obey Him.
4. Promote love and respect.
4. Maintain peace and order.
5. Protect people from wrongdoing.
6. Help people live good and responsible lives.
IMPORTANCE OF OBEYING GOD’S LAWS
Obeying God’s laws helps us to:
1. Please God.
2. Live peacefully with others.
3. Avoid wrongdoing.
4. Show love and respect.
5. Become responsible people.
6. Promote peace and justice.
Lesson - God is the giver of law, and His laws guide us to love God, obey Him, do what is right, and treat other people well.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Who is the giver of law to His people?
A. Abraham
B. God
C. Moses
D. David
2. What is a law?
A. An official instruction made by an authority
B. A game played by children
C. A story told in school
D. A song sung by pupils
3. What is a rule?
A. A punishment given to a person
B. A reward for good behaviour
C. A type of law made by God
D. An instruction that guides behaviour in a particular place or group
4. What can happen when a person breaks a law?
A. The person receives a gift
B. The person becomes a leader
C. The person may face legal punishment
D. The person receives praise
5. Why did God give laws to His people?
A. To cause confusion
B. To guide them to live rightly
C. To make them fight
D. To prevent them from helping others
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God is the giver of ______.
7. A law is an official ______ made by an authority.
8. Rules help to maintain ______ and order.
9. God’s laws teach people what is ______ and wrong.
10. The Ten Commandments were given to the Israelites through ______.
C. True or False
11. God gave laws to guide His people.
12. Rules can apply to a particular group or place.
13. Laws and rules have exactly the same purpose and application.
14. Breaking a law can lead to illegal punishment.
15. Disobeying laws helps to promote peace and order.
D. Matching
16. Ten Commandments - A. Instruction for a particular group or place
17. Moses - B. Official instruction made by an authority
18. Obedience - C. Led the Israelites when God gave the Ten Commandments
19. Rule - D. Laws given by God to the Israelites
20. Law - E. Doing what one is instructed to do
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. A 3. D 4. C 5. B
6. law
7. instruction
8. discipline
9. right
10. Moses
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. False
15. False
16. Ten Commandments - D. Laws given by God to the Israelites
17. Moses - C. Led the Israelites when God gave the Ten Commandments
18. Obedience - E. Doing what one is instructed to do
19. Rule - A. Instruction for a particular group or place
20. Law - B. Official instruction made by an authority
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that a law is an official instruction made by an authority to guide people’s behaviour and maintain order, while a rule is an instruction that guides behaviour in a particular place or situation. Laws and rules help people know what they should or should not do.
Pupils also learned that God gave laws to guide His people, teach them right from wrong, promote love and respect, maintain peace and order, and help them live good lives. We should obey God’s laws and lawful rules.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What is a law?
- What rules do we obey at home?
- What rules do we obey in school?
- Why should people obey laws and rules?
The teacher explains that laws and rules guide people’s behaviour and help society to live peacefully.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention some laws and rules they know.
Step 2: Meaning of Law
The teacher explains that a law is an official instruction or set of instructions made by an authority to guide people’s behaviour and maintain order.
The teacher explains that God’s laws are instructions given by God to guide His people to live according to His will.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of law in their own words.
Step 3: Meaning of Rules
The teacher explains that a rule is an instruction that tells people what they should or should not do in a particular place or situation.
Examples include:
- Obeying school regulations.
- Keeping the classroom clean.
- Raising your hand before speaking.
- Respecting teachers and other pupils.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention rules they follow at home and in school.
Step 4: Differences Between Laws and Rules
The teacher explains the differences:
- Laws are official instructions made by the government, while rules are instructions made by a school, family, organisation or group.
- Laws apply to people in a country, state or community, while rules apply to members of a particular group or people in a particular place.
- Breaking a law can lead to legal punishment, while breaking a rule leads to consequences set by the group or organisation.
- Laws maintain peace, order and justice in society, while rules maintain discipline and order in a particular place or group.
- Laws are enforced by government authorities, while rules are enforced by the authorities responsible for the group or place.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention differences between laws and rules.
Step 5: Why God Gave Laws
The teacher explains that God gave laws to:
- Guide His people.
- Teach people what is right and wrong.
- Help people obey Him.
- Promote love and respect.
- Maintain peace and order.
- Protect people from wrongdoing.
- Help people live good lives.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention reasons why God gave laws.
Step 6: Importance of Obeying Laws
The teacher explains that obeying laws helps to:
- Maintain peace and order.
- Protect people’s rights.
- Prevent wrongdoing.
- Promote justice.
- Encourage responsible behaviour.
- Make society safer.
The teacher reminds pupils that they should obey God’s laws as well as lawful rules and regulations.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention benefits of obeying laws and rules.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of law.
- Group 2: Explain the meaning of rules and give three examples.
- Group 3: Mention four differences between laws and rules.
- Group 4: Mention five reasons why God gave laws.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
Teacher’s Activities: The teacher reviews the meaning of law, meaning of rules, differences between laws and rules, and reasons why God gave laws. The teacher gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is a law?
2. What is a rule?
3. Mention three differences between laws and rules.
4. Mention five reasons why God gave laws.
5. State three benefits of obeying laws.

topics.content:
GOD CALL FOR A PURPOSE: PURPOSE OF GOD’S CALL, RESPONSE TO GOD’S CALL AND BENEFITS OF GOD’S CALL
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 6
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Calls His People: Why God Calls His People, Reasons for God’s Call, and the Call of Abraham | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 5 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD CALL FOR A PURPOSE
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of God Calls for a Purpose
2. Purposes of God’s Call
3. Response to God’s Call
4. Example: Abraham
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the purpose of God’s call.
2. Mention reasons why God calls His people.
3. Explain how to respond to God’s call.
4. Mention the benefits of responding to God’s call.
5. State lessons from people who responded to God’s call.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God calls His people to know Him, serve Him, obey His instructions and fulfil His plans.
They also learned about Abraham, who responded to God’s call by leaving his country as God instructed.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Pictures of people serving God
3. Bible story charts
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God calls people for different purposes. His call is not without a reason; He calls people to carry out His plans, serve Him and help others.
When God calls us, we should listen carefully, have faith, obey His instructions and be willing to do what He asks us to do. Responding positively to God’s call can bring blessings and help us fulfil His purpose.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the purpose of God’s call, how to respond to God’s call, and the benefits of responding to God’s call.
MEANING OF GOD CALLS FOR A PURPOSE
God calls His people for a specific reason or assignment. He calls people to know Him, serve Him, obey Him, fulfil His plans and help others.
God does not call people without a purpose. When He calls a person, He expects the person to listen, trust Him and carry out His instructions.
PURPOSES OF GOD’S CALL
God calls His people to:
1. Know and follow Him - To have a relationship with God.
2. Serve Him - To do God’s work and help others.
3. Obey His instructions - To follow what God commands.
4. Fulfil His plans - To carry out the work God has given them.
5. Help others - To care for and support people in need.
6. Lead others - To guide people in the right way.
7. Spread His message - To tell others about God’s word.
RESPONSE TO GOD’S CALL
When God calls us, we should:
1. Listen carefully.
2. Have faith in Him.
3. Obey His instructions.
4. Trust His promises.
5. Pray for guidance.
6. Be willing to serve.
7. Carry out His instructions.
BENEFITS OF RESPONDING TO GOD’S CALL
Responding positively to God’s call can:
1. Bring God’s blessings.
2. Strengthen our faith.
3. Help us fulfil God’s purpose.
4. Give us opportunities to serve others.
5. Make us useful to our families and communities.
6. Bring joy and satisfaction.
7. Help us develop a closer relationship with God.
Example: Abraham
Abraham responded to God’s call by leaving his country and relatives as God instructed him. He trusted God and obeyed His command.
Bible Reference: Genesis 12:1-9.
Lesson: We should listen to God, trust Him, obey His instructions and be willing to fulfil the purpose for which He calls us.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Why does God call His people?
A. To fulfil His purpose
B. To make them fight
C. To cause confusion
D. To make them unhappy
2. Which of these is a purpose of God’s call?
A. To disobey Him
B. To serve Him
C. To hate others
D. To cause trouble
3. How should we respond to God’s call?
A. By ignoring Him
B. By running away
C. By listening and obeying Him
D. By fighting others
4. Which of these is a benefit of responding to God’s call?
A. Hatred
B. Confusion
C. Disobedience
D. God’s blessings
5. Who responded to God’s call by leaving his country as God instructed?
A. Pilate
B. Pharaoh
C. Herod
D. Abraham
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God calls His people to fulfil His ______.

8. God calls people to ______ Him.

- What should a person do when God calls?

The teacher explains that God calls His people to:
- Know and follow Him.
- Serve Him.
- Obey His instructions.
- Fulfil His plans.
- Help other people.
- Lead others in the right way.
- Spread His message.

The teacher explains that responding to God’s call can:
- Bring God’s blessings.
- Help us fulfil God’s purpose.
- Strengthen our faith.
- Give us opportunities to serve others.
- Make us useful to our families and communities.
- Bring joy and satisfaction.
- Help us develop a closer relationship with God.

topics.content:

CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)

ENTRY BEHAVIOUR

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God calls His people to know Him, obey Him, serve Him and carry out His plans. Throughout the Bible, God called different people for special purposes and gave them instructions to follow.
When God calls a person, the person should listen, trust Him and obey His instructions. Abraham is an important example of someone who responded to God’s call with faith and obedience.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about why God calls His people, the reasons for God’s call, and the call of Abraham.
MEANING OF GOD CALLS HIS PEOPLE
God calls His people when He invites or instructs them to follow Him, serve Him, obey His instructions, or carry out a special purpose.
God can call people in different ways. His call may be through the Bible, prayer, dreams, visions, or through His servants.
WHY GOD CALLS HIS PEOPLE
God calls His people to:
1. Know Him - To understand and follow God.
2. Serve Him - To use their abilities to do God’s work.
3. Obey Him - To follow His instructions.
4. Fulfil His purpose - To carry out the work He has given them.
5. Help others - To care for and assist people in need.
6. Lead others - To guide people in the right way.
7. Spread His message - To tell others about God’s word.
HOW WE SHOULD RESPOND TO GOD’S CALL
When God calls us, we should:
1. Listen carefully.
2. Have faith in God.
3. Obey His instructions.
4. Trust His promises.
5. Be willing to serve Him.
6. Pray for guidance.
EXAMPLE OF GOD’S CALL
Abraham is an important example of someone God called. God told Abraham to leave his country, his relatives and his father’s household and go to a land that He would show him. Abraham obeyed God and went as instructed.
Bible Reference: Genesis 12:1-9.
Lesson - God calls people for different purposes. We should be willing to listen, trust, obey and serve God when He calls us.

Pupils learned that God calls His people to know Him, obey Him, serve Him and carry out His plans. God may call people to lead others, spread His message, help people and fulfil His purpose.
Pupils also learned about the call of Abraham. Abraham obeyed God and left his country as God instructed him. His response teaches us to have faith, trust God, obey His instructions and be patient.

The teacher asks pupils:

LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain how we are children of God.
2. Explain the meaning of being in Christ.

4. State ways family members can show love and care for one another.
5. Explain why Christians should live as children of God.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God speaks to people and that we should listen and obey Him.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils that God loves and cares for us as His children and expects us to live according to His ways.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every child belongs to a family and receives love, care and guidance from family members. In the same way, God loves, cares for and guides all people.
Being a child of God means accepting God, believing in Him and living according to His instructions. Christians are also called to live in Christ by following His teachings.
In this lesson, pupils will learn how we are children of God, the meaning of being in Christ and the characteristics of a model family.
LESSON 1 - HOW WE ARE CHILDREN OF GOD
We are children of God because God created us and loves us. He gives us life, cares for us and provides what we need.
We show that we are God’s children by believing in Him, loving others, obeying His commandments and doing what is right.
MEANING of BEING IN CHRIST
Being in Christ means believing in Jesus Christ, accepting Him and living according to His teachings.
A person who is in Christ should show love, kindness, forgiveness, honesty and obedience.
LESSON 2 - MEANING AND CHARACTERISTICS OF A MODEL FAMILY
A model family is a family where members live together in love, peace and unity.
The characteristics of a model family include:
1. Love - Family members care for and support one another.
2. Respect - Family members value and treat one another well.
3. Care - Family members look after one another.
4. Cooperation - Family members work together to achieve common goals.
5. Honesty - Family members tell the truth and avoid cheating.
6. Forgiveness - Family members forgive one another when they make mistakes.
7. Good Communication - Family members speak and listen to one another politely.
8. Obedience - Children follow the good instructions of their parents or guardians.

The teacher asks pupils:

ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God speaks to people in different ways and that God spoke to Jacob through a dream.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils the proper attitudes they should show when God speaks to them.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
When someone speaks to us, we are expected to listen carefully and respond appropriately. In the same way, when God speaks to us, we should pay attention and respond in the right way.
God speaks to guide, teach, warn, correct and encourage us. We should therefore show good attitudes when receiving His message.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of attitude, appropriate attitudes to show when God speaks to us, and reasons why God speaks to us.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF ATTITUDE
Attitude is the way a person thinks, feels or behaves towards someone or something.
When God speaks to us, we should have a good attitude by listening carefully and responding positively to His message.
APPROPRIATE ATTITUDES WHEN GOD SPEAKS TO US
We should show the following attitudes when God speaks to us:
1. Listening: We should listen carefully to God’s message.
2. Respect: We should treat God’s message with seriousness and respect.
3. Faith: We should believe and trust God.
4. Obedience: We should obey God’s instructions.
5. Humility: We should accept God’s instructions without pride.
6. Prayer: We should pray for understanding and guidance.
LESSON 2 - REASONS GOD SPEAKS TO US
God speaks to us to:
1. Guide us in the right way.
2. Teach us His ways.
3. Warn us against doing wrong.
4. Correct us when we make mistakes.
5. Encourage us when we are afraid or discouraged.
6. Reveal His plans and promises to us.
7. Help us obey His will and live a good life.

2. Mention ways through which God speaks to people.
3. State reasons why God speaks to people.
4. Explain how God spoke to Jacob.
5. State lessons learned from God’s communication with Jacob.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned that God created human beings and cares for them.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils how God communicates with people and why they should listen and respond to Him.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
People communicate with one another by speaking, writing, using signs and other means. In the same way, God communicates with people to guide, teach, warn and encourage them.
God can speak to people in different ways. In the Bible, God communicated with many people, including Jacob, to guide them and reveal His plans.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the ways through which God speaks to us, the purposes of God’s communication with us, and how God spoke to Jacob.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF GOD SPEAK TO US
God speaking to us means God communicating His message, guidance, instructions, or warnings to us.
WAYS THROUGH WHICH GOD SPEAKS TO US
God communicates with people in different ways. Some of the ways through which God speaks to us include:
1. Through the Bible: God speaks to us through His written Word and teaches us how to live.
2. Through Prayer: God can guide and answer us as we pray and listen to Him.
3. Through His Servants: God can use pastors, teachers and other people to deliver His message.
4. Through Dreams and Visions: In the Bible, God sometimes spoke to people through dreams and visions.
5. Through the Holy Spirit: The Holy Spirit guides, teaches and reminds believers of God’s ways.
6. Through Nature and Creation: God’s creation shows His power, wisdom and greatness.
LESSON 2 - PURPOSE OF GOD SPEAKING TO US
God speaks to us for different reasons. He speaks to:
1. Guide us in making good decisions.
2. Teach us His ways and commandments.
3. Warn us against doing wrong.
4. Correct us when we go astray.
5. Encourage us when we are afraid or discouraged.
6. Reveal His plans and promises to us.
7. Help us obey His will and live according to His instructions.
LESSON 3 - HOW GOD SPOKE TO JACOB
God spoke to Jacob when Jacob was travelling to Haran. At night, Jacob slept with a stone under his head. While sleeping, he had a dream.
In the dream, Jacob saw a ladder reaching from the earth to heaven, with angels going up and down on it. The Lord appeared to Jacob and spoke to him.
God promised Jacob that He would give him the land, bless him and his descendants, and be with him wherever he went. God also promised to protect him and bring him back safely.
Jacob woke up and realised that God had spoken to him. He was amazed and recognised that God was present in that place.

LEARNING OBJECTIVES

2. State the purposes of God’s revelation.

4. Mention ways God reveals Himself to His people.

6. Explain the importance of God’s revelation.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God gives laws to guide His people and help them live according to His will.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils how God makes Himself and His will known to His people.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God reveals Himself to people so that they can know Him, understand His will and follow His instructions. God’s revelation means the ways through which God makes Himself, His character, plans and messages known to people.
God revealed Himself to many people in the Bible. One example is Samuel, whom God called while he was serving in the temple under Eli.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the purpose of God’s revelation, the call of Samuel and the different ways God reveals Himself to His people.
MEANING OF GOD’S REVELATION
God’s revelation means God’s act of making Himself, His character, His will or His message known to people.
Through revelation, people can know more about God and understand what He wants them to do.
PURPOSE OF GOD’S REVELATION
God reveals Himself to people in order to:
1. Help people know Him.
2. Make His will known.
3. Guide His people.
4. Teach people what is right.
5. Warn people against wrongdoing.
6. Encourage and strengthen His people.
7. Reveal His plans and promises.
8. Help people obey and serve Him.
THE CALL OF SAMUEL
The story of Samuel’s call is recorded in 1 Samuel 3:1-21.
Samuel was a young boy who served God under Eli the priest. One night, while Samuel was sleeping in the temple near the Ark of God, the Lord called him.
Samuel answered, “Here I am.” He ran to Eli because he thought Eli had called him. Eli told him that he had not called him and asked him to go back and sleep.
The Lord called Samuel again, and Samuel went to Eli again. This happened three times.
Eli realised that it was the Lord who was calling Samuel. He instructed Samuel that if he heard the voice again, he should say, “Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.”
When the Lord called Samuel again, Samuel responded as Eli had instructed him. God then revealed His message to Samuel.
Samuel grew and became a prophet of God, and the Lord was with him.
WAYS GOD REVEALS HIMSELF TO HIS PEOPLE
God reveals Himself to His people in different ways, including:
1. The Bible: God reveals His character and will through His written Word.
2. Prayer: God can guide and communicate with people as they pray.
3. Dreams and visions: God sometimes used dreams and visions to communicate His messages.
4. His servants and prophets: God can deliver His message through people He chooses.
5. The Holy Spirit: The Holy Spirit guides and teaches believers.
6. Nature and creation: God’s creation shows His power, wisdom and greatness.
7. Jesus Christ: Christians believe God revealed Himself fully through Jesus Christ.
LESSONS FROM THE CALL OF SAMUEL
The call of Samuel teaches us to:
1. Listen carefully when God speaks.
2. Be willing to obey God’s instructions.
3. Respect godly guidance.
4. Be ready to serve God.
5. Respond to God with humility.
6. Trust God’s guidance.
7. Be faithful in our duties.
IMPORTANCE OF GOD’S REVELATION
God’s revelation is important because it:
1. Helps us know God.
2. Guides us in making right choices.
3. Teaches us God’s will.
4. Helps us avoid wrongdoing.
5. Strengthens our faith.
6. Encourages us to serve God.
7. Helps us live according to God’s purpose.

SUMMARY
God reveals Himself to people so that they can know Him, understand His will, receive guidance, and live according to His instructions. God can reveal Himself through the Bible, prayer, dreams and visions, His servants, the Holy Spirit, nature, and Jesus Christ.
Samuel was a young servant of God who was called by God while serving under Eli. He listened and responded, “Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.” His call teaches us to listen to God, obey His instructions, serve Him faithfully, and trust His guidance.
